sections.heading: AI governance: guardrails, cost and tracing
sections.body:
When AI applications use different tools and providers, security and engineering teams need a defined control point and a way to inspect usage. Linkfields AI Governance packages an AI gateway and governance layer built on **Portkey + Opik**.

Portkey and Opik are third-party components, not platforms owned by Linkfields. The Linkfields packaging, integration and governance configuration must be scoped alongside the underlying platform licences and operating responsibilities.

[Request an AI Governance walkthrough](#get-in-touch) · [View all products](/products-and-accelerators)
sections.secondaryHeading: Technical controls are not the whole governance programme
sections.secondaryBody:
This product sits in [Cyber Security](/services/cyber-security). It is distinct from [AI strategy & governance](/services/data-ai/ai-strategy-governance), which addresses use-case priorities, ownership and organisational governance.

For security control design and GRC support, explore [AI security & GRC](/services/cyber-security/ai-security-grc). A gateway alone does not establish legal or regulatory compliance.

sections.heading: Three governance priorities
sections.description: The product offer covers guardrails, cost and tracing. Start with the controls and evidence your AI workload needs, then establish the supported configuration.

items.title: Guardrails
items.description: Translate AI-use rules into a control checklist: what should be permitted, restricted or reviewed. Demonstrate the relevant gateway behaviour before approving the configuration.
items.bullets:
Input – agreed AI-use policies
Evaluation output – policy tests and supported-control scope

items.title: Cost visibility
items.description: Use cost visibility to assess the spend associated with the agreed AI workload. Confirm the available usage views and attribution detail rather than assume universal budget enforcement.
items.bullets:
Input – workload and cost-review needs
Evaluation output – usage views and review responsibilities

items.title: Tracing
items.description: Inspect the path of an AI interaction to understand how the workload behaves. Agree which trace evidence is needed and who may inspect prompt and response content.
items.bullets:
Input – sample interactions and evidence needs
Evaluation output – trace coverage and data-handling rules

sections.heading: Evaluate the gateway in your AI estate
sections.description: Evaluation workflow, not a production architecture: agree the application, gateway, model/provider and tracing paths for one workload before expanding coverage.

items.title: Map the workload
items.description: Identify the application, AI tools, model providers and data types. Record trust boundaries and the current operating owners.

items.title: Scope the stack
items.description: Confirm what Portkey + Opik provide and what Linkfields configures or integrates. Check provider coverage and third-party terms.

items.title: Test the controls
items.description: Use agreed sample interactions to inspect guardrail behaviour, usage visibility and trace evidence. Include failure-handling questions.

items.title: Agree operation
items.description: Set access, secrets, retention and incident responsibilities. Accept the design only against the controls actually demonstrated.

sections.heading: Example: a governed knowledge assistant
sections.body:
**Example engagement pattern, not a client case study.** An enterprise team wants to introduce a knowledge assistant but first needs visibility of its AI interactions. Start with one workload, agreed sample prompts and a named control owner.

The evaluation produces an application-to-gateway map, a supported-control checklist, sample usage and trace evidence, and a responsibility matrix. Organisational policy and security review remain separate from the technical gateway configuration.

For the wider evidence and remediation programme, explore [Regulated Cyber Readiness](/solutions/regulated-cyber-readiness).

sections.heading: Agree the technical and commercial boundary
sections.description: Available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without Linkfields services. A walkthrough should establish the Linkfields scope, third-party terms and supported estate before procurement.

items.title: What is included, and who owns it?
items.description: AI Governance is the Linkfields-packaged offer built on Portkey + Opik. Agree and document in the proposal the Linkfields layer, underlying platform editions and licences, configuration artefacts, optional services and each party’s support responsibility. Do not treat third-party technology as Linkfields-owned IP.

items.title: Which tools and integrations fit?
items.description: Bring your application and provider inventory. Establish supported models, tools, connection paths and trace coverage in the evaluation. Specify integration effort, request behaviour and failure or failover handling; coverage is not assumed for every AI tool.

items.title: Where does it run, and what is logged?
items.description: Agree the available hosting model, region and data residency before selecting deployment. Review prompt and response retention, redaction, access controls, secrets handling and model-provider data use. Record the trust boundaries and approval owners.

items.title: How do we buy and operate it?
items.description: Separate Linkfields licence or subscription terms from SaaS hosting, third-party fees and optional implementation or managed support. Confirm availability, version, onboarding, release responsibilities, support scope and any agreed service levels explicitly in the proposal. This page does not imply a service-level commitment.
